exposure: perinatal follow-up status (prenatal follow-up, born without follow-up at study hospital, accepted from external centers)
cohort: The study included 280 term neonates diagnosed with critical congenital heart disease (CCHD), monitored in the neonatology and pediatric cardiac intensive care unit between January 1, 2023, and January 1, 2024.
finding: Neonatal morbidity (22% vs. 25% vs. 36%) and mortality rates (6% vs. 9% vs. 18%) were lower in neonates with prenatal follow-up (Group I) and those born without follow-up at the study hospital (Group II) compared to those accepted from external centers (Group III) after interventional or surgical procedures.
mod_finding: The cesarean section rate was higher in the prenatal follow-up group (Group I) at 80% compared to 52% in Group II and 45% in Group III.
